description: Critical evolutionary markers of the Indian Constitution. The 42nd and 44th Amendments significantly restructured executive powers and citizen obligations, while the 73rd and 74th Amendments legally decentralized democracy through local self-governments.

sections.title: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
sections.description: Enacted by the Indira Gandhi government during the National Emergency, it is the most comprehensive amendment in Indian history, famously known as the 'Mini-Constitution'.

key_concepts.explanation: The committee whose recommendations formed the operational basis for inserting Fundamental Duties into the constitutional framework.

polity_articles.provision: Amended the structural preamble of India for the first and only time.
polity_articles.details: Added three new definitive terms: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.
Incorporated a list of 10 non-justiciable Fundamental Duties for citizens, heavily inspired by the USSR constitution.

polity_articles.provision: Expanded the mandate of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
polity_articles.details: Added Article 39A (Equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (Participation of workers in management of industries), and Article 48A (Protection of environment, forests, and wildlife).

sections.title: 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978
sections.description: Introduced by the Morarji Desai-led Janata Party government to reverse several authoritarian modifications introduced by the 42nd Amendment and safeguard democratic checks and balances.

polity_articles.provision: Stripped the Right to Property of its status as a fundamental guarantee.
polity_articles.details: Removed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, reclassifying it as a mere legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

polity_articles.provision: Imposed strict procedural safe-guards on declaring a National Emergency.
polity_articles.details: Substituted the subjective phrase 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'. Mandated that the President can only proclaim an emergency upon receiving a written recommendation from the Cabinet.
Empowered the President to send ministerial advice back to the Cabinet once for reconsideration. However, the reconsidered advice was made strictly binding.

polity_articles.provision: Protected crucial fundamental rights during national crises.
polity_articles.details: Declared that the right to protection in respect of conviction for offenses (Article 20) and the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21) cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

sections.title: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
sections.description: Institutionalized rural local self-governments, establishing statutory uniformity for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) across the country.

key_concepts.explanation: Mandated a uniform hierarchy: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the intermediate/block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.

polity_articles.provision: Inserted a dedicated constitutional segment titled 'The Panchayats'.
polity_articles.details: Constitutionalized the Gram Sabha as the foundational body, institutionalized mandatory direct elections, and fixed a minimum of 1/3rd seat reservation for women across all tiers.

polity_articles.provision: Created a dedicated functional roster for rural local governance.
polity_articles.details: Allocated 29 functional matters (e.g., agriculture, land improvement, minor irrigation) over which Panchayats hold executive powers.

polity_articles.provision: Setup sovereign supportive institutions for local bodies.
polity_articles.details: Article 243I mandated the State Finance Commission to manage fiscal distribution, and Article 243K created the State Election Commission to conduct free and independent local polls.

sections.title: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
sections.description: Constitutionalized urban local self-government structures, creating an institutional framework for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).

key_concepts.explanation: Categorized urban centers into three distinct administrative bodies: Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas, and Municipal Corporations for large metropolitan zones.

polity_articles.provision: Inserted a new administrative segment titled 'The Municipalities'.
polity_articles.details: Provided statutory backing for setting up Ward Committees, and mandated seat reservations for SC/ST and women in urban administrations.

polity_articles.provision: Created a dedicated functional roster for urban local governance.
polity_articles.details: Enlisted 18 distinct functional matters under the domain of Municipalities, covering urban planning, roads, bridges, and public health systems.
Mandated the formation of a District Planning Committee (DPC) in every state to consolidate developmental drafts prepared by both rural Panchayats and urban Municipalities.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: High-yield factual pointers frequently tested in competitive examinations regarding historical context and timelines.

important_facts.fact: Both the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts were passed during the prime ministerial tenure of P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The 73rd Amendment came into effect on April 24, 1993, which is why April 24 is celebrated nationally as National Panchayati Raj Day.
Madhya Pradesh was the very first state to hold democratic elections under the revamped guidelines of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act.
The 42nd Amendment had extended the institutional tenure of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 5 to 6 years, a change that was promptly rolled back to 5 years by the 44th Amendment.
